title: MOSFET Scaling Simulator
description: A trend model of MOSFET scaling from a 1 micrometer, 5 V reference transistor down to a 5 nm gate. A cross section and a gate-control gauge show the chosen architecture (planar bulk, FDSOI, FinFET, or gate-all-around nanowire). One plot shows DIBL, threshold voltage roll-off, and subthreshold slope against gate length. A second plot shows switching speed, dynamic power density, and leakage power density, with the constant-field (Dennard) and constant-voltage regions shaded.

chapter_title: Short-Channel Effects, CMOS, and Advanced FET Structures

educational.topic: MOSFET scaling, short-channel effects, and advanced transistor architectures
learningObjectives: Identify which short-channel effects appear as the gate length is reduced
Calculate the dynamic power dissipation for a given frequency and activity factor
Explain why a FinFET gives better electrostatic control than a planar MOSFET
Compare the trade-offs between the advanced FET architectures
prerequisites: The long-channel MOSFET, threshold voltage, and subthreshold slope
Short-channel effects, CMOS power, and Dennard scaling

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Gate length and supply sliders with an architecture menu, two linked log-log plots, a cross section with a gate-control gauge, and a readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe, followed by a comparison table that students fill in across the four architectures
assessmentOpportunities: Find the shortest gate length that keeps DIBL under 50 mV/V for each architecture
Explain the slope of the dynamic power curve in the two scaling regions
Compute dynamic power from the activity factor, capacitance, supply voltage, and frequency

equations: Natural length: planar sqrt(3 t_ox t_dep); FDSOI sqrt(3 t_ox t_si); FinFET sqrt(3 t_ox t_fin / 2); GAA (R/2) sqrt(3)
theta = exp(-L / (2 lambda)); DIBL = theta; Delta V_T = -(V_DS + 0.4 V) theta
Reference scaling: t_ox = L/50, t_dep = L/7, V_DD = 5 V L / 1 um, V_T = V_DD/4, with floors
P_dyn = alpha C V_DD^2 f; P_leak = I_off V_DD; I_off = 100 nA (W/L) 10^(-V_T,eff/S)
assumptions: Floors: t_ox >= 1 nm, t_dep >= 12 nm, V_DD >= slider value
FDSOI film 6 nm, fin width 6 nm, nanowire diameter 5 nm at every gate length
Velocity-saturated on-current with v_sat = 1e7 cm/s; clock period of 20 gate delays; activity factor 0.1
limitations: Illustrative trend model; not calibrated to any commercial process and not labeled with node names
Uniform channel doping for planar bulk; no halo implants or shallow-junction effects
Subthreshold leakage only; no gate tunneling or junction leakage
